findings.asked: Timetable arithmetic, then an average speed in miles per hour.
findings.wentWrong: Time was handled in tens rather than sixties; many got 85 instead of 45 minutes; of those with the right time, only the best converted to hours - most divided 54 by 45.
findings.rule: Convert minutes to hours (divide by 60) before dividing distance by time.

findings.asked: Average speed over two legs with different speeds and times.
findings.wentWrong: The weakest added the two speeds and halved; better candidates reached 57 miles in 90 minutes and then stumbled on the time conversion.
findings.rule: Average speed = total distance / total time - never the mean of the speeds.

ruleToRemember: Average speed = total distance divided by total time, with time in hours (minutes divided by 60); averaging two speeds is wrong unless the times are equal.
